solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Psychiatrist's technique revealed in brief conversation with union

parts.note: to have a word with someone is to have a brief conversation
an association is a union or league of members

explanation.surface: A therapist's method turns out to come from a quick chat with a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' and 'with' are link words; the union sounds like a trade union but is just a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: In this psychological test a patient replies to each prompt with the first word that comes to mind.

clue.text: Artist not finished? Blow me!

indicators.note: an unfinished word loses its last letter, here taken from the painter's name

parts.note: James Whistler was an American-born painter

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about a painter who never completed his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' drops the final R from WHISTLER. 'Blow me!' is an exclamation of surprise, like a low whistle of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: A low whistle is the sound people make in astonishment, much as they might exclaim the idiom blow me.

clue.text: Page clergyman shortened

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its tail, here the last letter of the parish priest

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar has had his sermon page cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' removes the final R from RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book is called the recto, the opposite of verso.

clue.text: Sit with Santa's new helper

indicators.note: making something new out of these letters means rearranging them

parts.note: the possessive is spelt out here, its S included in the letters

explanation.surface: A child is told to sit beside Father Christmas's latest elf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal; the possessive S of Santa's is needed as a letter here, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide or assistant is someone who helps another person in their work.

clue.text: Sounds like Twist, for example, revolting Dickensian character?

indicators.note: the clue says a word for twist is to be said aloud and heard, not spelt

parts.note: to screw something is to twist it

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist is offered as an example of a disgusting character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' pretends to be Oliver Twist. 'revolting' turns EG into GE, and the sound of SCREW gives SCROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer is the miserly central figure of Dickens's novella A Christmas Carol.

clue.text: Praise expert on horseback

parts.note: a crack shot or crack player is an expert one
a jockey who is up is mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: Applause for a skilled rider sitting on his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' meaning riding is a racing term: the jockey named as 'up' is the one in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk something up glowingly is to praise it, as in the phrase it is not all it is cracked up to be.

clue.text: A head of Rugby understood slang

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so got means understood

explanation.surface: A Rugby School headmaster could follow the pupils' slang.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a famous English public school as well as the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is jargon or slang peculiar to a particular group of people.

clue.text: I will cure half of this sickness

parts.note: contracted, I will becomes I'll
to heal is to cure

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone promises to cure part of this illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of this' gives TH, the front half of THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor health is a state of being unwell, so it means the same as sickness.

clue.text: Garden centre in Surrey, busy after noon

indicators.note: the rearranged county comes after the single letter in the answer
busy suggests bustling activity, so the county's letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A Surrey garden centre gets crowded in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London. 'busy' makes URSERY from the county, set 'after' the abbreviation for noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery raises and sells young plants, just like a garden centre.

clue.text: In front of chops is gold tooth

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gold tooth sits at the front of someone's jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chops' are jaws, which suits the tooth, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the front cutting teeth.

clue.text: Bony, a maltreated langur

indicators.note: something maltreated is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skinny monkey has been treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A langur is an Asian monkey; 'maltreated' rearranges A LANGUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes a lean body with sharp, jutting bones.

clue.text: Assessed situation and bought shares

definitions.meaning: to take stock is to review how matters stand
taking stock can literally mean acquiring stocks or shares

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pausing to assess things, while read literally it means acquiring shares or goods.

clue.text: Subject, English, to be set by those people

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed beside the pronoun, after it in the answer

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: An English topic is to be chosen by certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Soldiers beheaded and left in hollow in surrounded area

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: Decapitated troops are abandoned in a cave inside a besieged zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' leaves EN from the soldiers; 'in' places the letter for left inside the hollow, giving CLAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly enclosed within another state's land.

clue.text: Footwear item, the type Venus Williams might wear?

definitions.meaning: a plain low-cut women's shoe with a heel

definitions.text: the type Venus Williams might wear
definitions.meaning: a tennis star plays on a court

explanation.walkthrough: Venus Williams is a champion tennis player, which invites reading the phrase literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This pump-style shoe has a low cut and no fastening, and the name also suits tennis wear.

clue.text: Talk about southern herb

indicators.note: the talk goes around the letter for southern

parts.note: a parley is a talk, especially between enemies

explanation.surface: A conversation about a herb grown in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside PARLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common culinary herb with curly or flat leaves.

clue.text: Carpet salesman, guy let in free

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: the man is let in, placed inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A carpet seller lets a man come in without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, not a floor covering: to be carpeted is to be called in and scolded. 'let in' gives RIMAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called in for a scolding, so the verb means to rebuke.

clue.text: Small mollusc in sink

parts.note: the cuttle or cuttlefish is a mollusc

explanation.surface: A little shellfish is found in a kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' is the verb: to scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuttling a vessel means sinking it on purpose by holing it.

clue.text: Gag made by the Italian during comic scene

indicators.note: the article goes in the middle of the jumbled word
comic suggests a farce, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian actor tells a joke during a funny scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but is a verb. 'comic' makes SENCE, and 'during' sets the Italian article inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to stop them speaking, which is what silencing them means.

clue.text: Stop — proceed after amber changes

indicators.note: the word for proceed follows the jumbled colour in the answer
when something changes its form the letters are rearranged

parts.note: go means proceed

explanation.surface: A driver goes when the traffic light changes from amber.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a traffic light; 'changes' makes EMBAR from the colour, and 'after' puts the word for proceed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban that halts trade, a stop on it.

clue.text: Truncheon around back of hip brought to work in police station

indicators.note: the club goes around the end letter of hip

parts.note: a cosh is a short heavy club

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A truncheon is carried at the hip to work at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps COSH round P (from 'back of hip'). COP SHOP is British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a station house where officers work is called by this slang term.

clue.text: All the players holding an ace in card game

indicators.note: the cast holds the little word inside it

parts.note: the cast is all the players in a production
A is the abbreviation for ace on a playing card

explanation.surface: Every player in a card game is holding an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' gives CANAST, the little word sitting just after the first letter of the players' word; the ace comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Salesman's talk on new model

parts.note: patter is the smooth talk of a salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman delivers his spiel about a new model.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to be copied.

clue.text: Lock in criminal at chokey

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of these words, read across the spaces

explanation.surface: A lock is fitted on a criminal's prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters run inside criminAL AT CHokey. Chokey is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple fastening for a door, a kind of lock.

clue.text: Opening of historical play inaccurately portrayed? It may be

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
something portrayed inaccurately is distorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A history play may well present events wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurately portrayed' makes APLY. The definition is an archaic adverb, so read 'It may be' as perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Haply is an old word for perhaps, which is the sense of the phrase it may be.

clue.text: Hedonist, tense after examination in German city

indicators.note: the letter for tense comes after the rest
the oral test goes inside the city

parts.note: Bonn is a German city, once the West German capital
a viva is an oral university examination
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker gets nervous after an exam in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous but is T. 'in' gives BONVIVAN, and 'after' adds the T at the end; a viva is a British oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant is someone who enjoys good food, drink and pleasure.

clue.text: The full version of Beethoven's Fifth?

definitions.text: The full version of Beethoven's Fifth

parts.words: The full version of Beethoven's Fifth
parts.note: the fifth letter of the composer's name is H, and the full version is how that letter's name is spelt out

explanation.walkthrough: The Fifth sounds like the symphony, but it is the fifth letter of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H, written as a word, is spelt out in full this way.

clue.text: Phone nervously about outsider's first run — rank outsider

indicators.note: the jumbled phone goes around the first letter
done nervously, the letters are jumbled
the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A nervous call is made about the leading runner, an unlikely winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' turns PHONE into NHOPE; 'about' puts O inside it (NOHOPE), then R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success is a hopeless case, like a rank outsider in a race.

clue.text: Establish colony around a US port

indicators.note: the word for establishing a colony goes around the letter A

parts.note: to settle a place is to found a colony there

explanation.surface: Settlers found a colony round an American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps SETTLE round A.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Washington State is a major Pacific seaport.

clue.text: The navy renowned at sea? Not all of the time

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The famous navy is out at sea, but not constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the navy but signals the letters of THE NAVY RENOWNED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, at intervals, so not all the time.
